key_insight: Metal choice controls direct light-induced charge injection into adsorbed CO, with electron injection exceeding hole injection across all nine metals studied.
engineering_relevance: Selecting suitable metals and adsorbate energy-level alignment could guide nanoscale photocatalyst design while bypassing rapid hot-carrier thermalization.
method: Model CO–metal interactions using ab initio density functional theory.
Describe localized surface plasmons using macroscopic electrodynamics.
Predict electron and hole injection rates from large spherical nanoparticles.
evidence_signal: Across nine metals, Al, Ag, Cu and Au yielded the largest electron injection rates at optical photon energies, with significant plasmonic enhancement for Cu and Au.
watch_item: The predictions concern CO on large spherical nanoparticles; applicability to other adsorbates or particle geometries requires further evaluation.
paper_title: Material dependence of direct light-induced charge injection from metallic nanoparticles into adsorbates
